documents.title: Quarterly Coordination Meeting – Facilitator Notes
documents.content:
Meeting opened 09:35. S.O welcomed everyone, noted this is the first quarterly meeting for 2023 with the new access planning system in place since January. Purpose of today: confirm roles and responsibilities for the coming maintenance window (April–June), review the pre-Christmas shutdown learnings, and set the agenda for the winter works program.

---

**2. Review of Previous Actions (from December 2022 meeting)**

- **SB12 – Sleeper replacement at Kariong** – Completed 19/12/2022. R. Singh confirmed final inspection passed. No further action.
- **OHW clearance near Gosford station** – P. Delaney advised still open. Vegetation team scheduled for late March. **Action: P.D to confirm date with contractor by 24/03.**
- **Access planning template** – A. Kaur circulated new template in January. All supervisors to use for April window. **Action: All to confirm receipt by end of week.**

---

**3. Roles & Responsibilities – Confirmation for 2023–24**

S.O opened discussion on roles. Noted that some confusion had arisen during the summer heat restrictions about who coordinates emergency access outside normal planning hours.

Discussion points:
- R. Singh confirmed that for track maintenance, the on-call supervisor retains authority for emergency track possessions. However, any works affecting platform areas must be cleared with H. Nakamura's team first.
- J. Whitfield raised the point about rolling stock movements during night works – the interface role is to confirm no stabled trains are in the affected sidings. This is currently done via email, but J.W suggested a shared checklist.
- P. Delaney noted that for OHW isolations, the request must come through the planning team (A. Kaur) at least 5 working days prior. This was agreed in the December meeting but not always followed.
- A. Kaur confirmed that the new access planning system flags conflicting requests automatically. However, it does not yet flag conflicts with platform works – that is still a manual check. **Action: A.K to raise this with IT as a system enhancement request.**

**Decision:** For the April–June window, the following roles are confirmed and recorded as current:

- **Track Maintenance Requests** – R. Singh (primary), D. Osei (secondary for night shifts)
- **Signals & Comms** – L. Petrov
- **OHW Isolations** – P. Delaney (must be lodged via planning team)
- **Rolling Stock Interface** – J. Whitfield
- **Access Planning & Scheduling** – A. Kaur
- **Safety & Compliance Review** – M. Tran
- **Meeting Facilitation & Action Tracking** – Sarah O'Connor, Facilitator

*Note: Sarah O'Connor's role_title is Facilitator as noted in the facilitator notes. Record status: current. This remains the current arrangement for all quarterly coordination meetings.*

No objections raised. Roles recorded in the shared drive under "2023_Quarterly_Roles_v1.xlsx".

---

**4. Pre-Christmas Shutdown – Lessons Learned**

R. Singh provided a summary of the shutdown (18–24 December 2022). Key points:

- Overall, works completed on time. Two items slipped: the footpath resurfacing near Woy Woy station (delayed due to weather) and a signal cable replacement at Tuggerah (parts issue).
- The footpath work has been rescheduled for the April window. Bitumen work requires dry conditions – noted as a risk for autumn.
- Communication during the shutdown was generally good, but there was one instance where the night crew (D. Osei) was not copied into a final possession change. This caused a 45-minute delay. **Action: M.T to add a checklist item for "all shift leads copied on possession changes" to the shutdown protocol.**

L. Petrov raised a concern about the handover process – the day crew and night crew used different log formats. This was resolved informally on the day but should be formalised. **Action: L.P to draft a standard handover template by 31/03.**

---

**5. April–June Maintenance Window – Draft Schedule**

A. Kaur presented the draft schedule. Key dates:

- **Week 1 (3–7 April):** Sleeper replacement – Gosford to Narara. Night works, 4 possessions.
- **Week 2 (10–14 April):** OHW inspection – Ourimbah. Day works, requires 2 isolations.
- **Week 3 (17–21 April):** Signal cable replacement – Tuggerah (carryover from shutdown).
- **Week 4 (24–28 April):** Platform edge painting – Woy Woy. Requires interface with station operations.
- **May:** No major works scheduled yet – awaiting confirmation on funding for ballast cleaning.
- **June:** Pre-winter inspection program – all crews.

**7. Resource Planning – Inspection Team Capacity**

A. Kaur presented a capacity summary for the Track Inspection Team for the April–June period.

- The team has 6 qualified inspectors, with 2 additional inspectors in training (both expected to be signed off by mid-May).

The group agreed to keep the 14-day cycle and to review resourcing if the ballast cleaning was confirmed.

*Note: The resource plan is to be updated once funding for ballast cleaning is confirmed. A. Kaur to flag this at the next coordination call.*

---

**9. Inspection Findings – Recent Issues**

A. Kaur provided a brief update on recent inspection findings from the last two cycles.

- **Site: Gosford to Narara (sleeper replacement area)** – Two loose sleepers identified during the inspection on 08/03. These were in the area scheduled for replacement in April. The sleepers have been marked and will be addressed during the possession. No immediate action required.
- **Site: Ourimbah (OHW)** – No significant findings. One insulator crack noted, scheduled for replacement during the April OHW inspection.
- **Site: Woy Woy (platform edge)** – Minor spalling on the platform edge, consistent with previous reports. No change in condition since the last inspection.
- **Site: Tuggerah (signal cable route)** – The cable route was inspected on 10/03. No issues found in the section where the cable replacement is scheduled.
- **Site: Narara (level crossing)** – Flooding debris was noted near the crossing after recent rain. The drainage pit was cleared by the track crew on 13/03. The inspection team will re-check on the next cycle.

R. Singh noted that the inspection findings were consistent with the expected condition of the assets and did not indicate any systemic issues. The group agreed that the 14-day frequency was providing adequate coverage.

---

**10. Any Other Business**

- M. Tran reminded the group that the quarterly safety statistics report was due by 31/03. A. Kaur to submit the inspection-related data by 28/03.

- R. Singh noted that the next coordination call was scheduled for 28/03 and that the April window briefing would be held on 31/03.

The Quarterly Coordination Meeting's meeting frequency remains 3 months, with the current arrangement confirmed as the standing cadence. A trial of the pre-possession coordination call (Option C) will proceed for the next two major windows (May and July 2024), with a review at the August meeting.

- **Scheduling note for the next meeting:** The August session is proposed for Wednesday 14/08/2024, subject to room availability at the Hornsby depot. A calendar invite will be sent by 31/05.

- S. O'Connor summarised the written feedback received from attendees following the February meeting. A total of 9 responses were returned (out of 16 invited).

- **Common themes from the feedback:**
  - *Action tracking:* Several respondents noted that actions are not always closed out between meetings, and that there is no single visible register of open items. One comment read: "actions seem to disappear after the minutes are sent."
  - *Possession planning:* Three respondents requested earlier visibility of the draft possession plan, so that local teams can flag conflicts sooner.
  - *Communications:* Two respondents asked for a simpler distribution list for program updates, rather than receiving multiple separate emails from different teams.

Quarterly Coordination Meeting's meeting_frequency_months is 3 months as noted in the facilitator notes. Record status: current.

  - A single weekly program update email, consolidating track, sleeper, OHW, and signal items, to replace the separate updates currently sent by each discipline lead.

O'Connor confirmed it would be shared with the program team distribution list, but that external stakeholders would only receive a summary.
